transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time from patients with more serious problems, but... well, I suppose I just needed a little advice. It's a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, really, because I'm usually perfectly fine and independent. 

It's just... what finally made me come in is that the moment my car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami, I get this... this silly overreaction. My chest tightens up terribly, and my hands just clamp down on the steering wheel. I get this sudden, absolute certainty that I have to get off the bridge right that second, even though, you know, there’s nowhere to go. I try to tell myself it's fine and not to make a fuss, but the feeling is just so strong. 

I know it sounds a bit foolish... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Do you ever experience these kinds of feelings—like chest tightness, fear of not being able to escape—anywhere else, or is it only when you're on bridges?

Oh, no, no. Goodness, no. It really is just the bridges. I'm quite alright everywhere else, I promise. 

I go about my normal day—driving to the grocery store, visiting my friends, running errands—and I'm perfectly fine. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or that I'm just generally a nervous person, because I'm really not. It's just... well, just that one specific, silly thing with those long bridges over the water. 

I hope that's helpful for you? I'd hate to be a complicated case for you to figure out.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that peaked within minutes, even when you weren't on a bridge?

Oh, no, Doctor. No, nothing like that. I don't just... get frightened out of the blue. I'd be terribly embarrassed if I did! 

Sitting at home, or out to lunch with the girls, I'm right as rain. It truly is just when I'm driving up onto one of those awful bridges. I've never had one of those sudden spells you're describing just out of nowhere. 

I hope that makes sense? I really am quite a sensible person otherwise, I promise you.
When you think about driving over those long bridges, do you ever avoid them altogether, even if you're not feeling the chest tightness or fear at that exact moment?

Well... yes, I suppose I do. I try not to let it interfere too much, of course, because I don't want to be a bother to anyone. But lately... well, I've actually started turning down a few things. 

Just silly little things, really! Like... oh, gallery openings, or those birdwatching trips I used to enjoy so much. And... well, even some visits with my daughter, unless someone else is available to drive me over the water. 

It’s terribly embarrassing to admit, Doctor. I’ve always been the one who planned everything and handled things myself, you know? I hate the idea of relying on others just because I'm being foolish about a bridge. I hope you don't think less of me for it... I really do try my best to be independent. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
